title: A gift for someone who has everything
body:
Why it is so hard

Some people are impossible to buy for. Not because they are difficult, but because they already own the good headphones, the nice candle and the bottle of wine you were thinking of. Anything you can find in a shop, they could have bought themselves, and probably did.

The answer is a gift they could not have bought, because it only exists because of you. That means something personal, something to do together, or something that tells their own story back to them.

Three questions that help

  • Which place do they always talk about? The city where they studied, the village of their grandparents, the beach of every summer.
  • What would they never buy for themselves? Often something small and a little indulgent, or something purely sentimental.
  • What did you do together that you both still mention? A trip, a concert, a first meeting.

Seven ideas

  1. A map of their place. The street they grew up in, the city where they fell in love or the town they keep going back to, with a pin on the exact spot.
  2. A day instead of a thing. A walk, a lunch and a museum in a city they love, planned completely by you.
  3. A letter. Write down what they mean to you. It costs nothing and it is the gift people keep longest.
  4. A restored favourite. Have their old watch serviced, their favourite bag repaired or a photo from a shoebox printed and framed.
  5. A lesson with a master. A workshop in something they love: bread, pottery, wine, photography.
  6. Their story, written down. For a parent or grandparent: a book of questions about their life, to fill in and give back.
  7. A donation in their name. To a cause they care about, with a card that explains why you chose it.

Why a map works so well

A map print is one of the few things on this list that is both personal and beautiful enough for the wall of someone with taste. It shows a place they know by heart, in a way they have never seen it. And it cannot be bought in a shop, because it is made for one address and one story.

How to make it theirs

  • Choose the place. Search any address in the world and zoom until the streets look right.
  • Mark the spot. A heart, a star or a small house on the place that matters.
  • Write the words. The name of the place, a date or a single line that only they will understand.
  • Match their home. Choose a palette and a frame that suit their interior. When in doubt, a calm palette with a black or natural wood frame fits almost everywhere.

Not sure about the size? Our guide to sizes and frames shows every option to scale, and our city map prints are a good place to start looking.
summary: They buy what they need the moment they need it, so every object you think of is already in the cupboard. The way out is not a better thing, but a better story. Seven ideas that work.
